definitions.explanation: A place where a road crosses a railway track at the same level, typically with barriers and warning signals.

examples.japanese: {踏切|ふみきり}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{電車|でんしゃ}→電車：00522_densha⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{待|ま}った→待つ：00469_matsu⟧。
examples.english: I waited at the railroad crossing for the train to pass.

examples.japanese: {踏切|ふみきり}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{遮断機|しゃだんき}→遮断機：16229_shadanki⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{降|お}りて→降りる：00568_oriru⟧⟦きた→来る：00254_kuru⟧。
{踏切|ふみきり}⟦{事故|じこ}→事故：00851_jiko⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{注意|ちゅうい}→注意：01464_chuui⟧⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧⟦ください→ください：02899_kudasai⟧。
examples.english: Please be careful of accidents at railroad crossings.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{道|みち}→道：00505_michi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{踏切|ふみきり}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{多|おお}くて→多い：01127_ooi⟧⟦{渋滞|じゅうたい}→渋滞：03279_juutai⟧⟦しやすい→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: This road has many railroad crossings and tends to get congested.

notes:
COMPOSITION: {踏|ふ}む (to step) + {切|き}る (to cross/cut) = stepping across the tracks

RAILROAD CROSSING COMPONENTS:
- {遮断機|しゃだんき} - crossing barrier/gate
- {警報機|けいほうき} - warning signal/alarm
- {踏切|ふみきり}{警報|けいほう}{音|おん} - crossing warning sound (the distinctive カンカンカン sound)

SAFETY TERMS:
- {踏切|ふみきり}{事故|じこ} - railroad crossing accident
- {踏切|ふみきり}{内|ない}に{閉|と}じ{込|こ}められる - to be trapped inside the crossing
- {非常|ひじょう}ボタン - emergency button

TYPES OF CROSSINGS:
- {第一種踏切|だいいっしゅふみきり} - first-class crossing (with barriers and alarms)
- {第四種踏切|だいよんしゅふみきり} - fourth-class crossing (no barriers, warning signs only)

RELATED INFRASTRUCTURE:
- {高架|こうか} - elevated railway/overpass
- {地下道|ちかどう} - underground passage
- {歩道橋|ほどうきょう} - pedestrian overpass
